original_question: For an F-division algebra A of degree n, what is the smallest finite group that can occur as the Galois group of the Galois closure of a maximal subfield of A? In particular, does every degree-n division algebra have a separable maximal subfield whose Galois closure has Galois group the alternating group A_n?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Other problems regarding crossed products," specifically Problem 2.4 in the subsection "Smallest Galois splitting fields."
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient object (an F-division algebra of degree n), the relevant Galois-theoretic construction (the Galois closure of a maximal subfield), and the paper’s singled-out special case asking whether the alternating group A_n can occur. It also stays on the exact problem in the paper rather than drifting to the neighboring abelian-splitting question (Problem 2.5) or the broader admissibility problem.
missing_details: The paper formulates this in terms of the "smallest splitting group(s)," so the group should be understood as a finite Galois group of a splitting field of A arising specifically from the Galois closure of a maximal subfield.

The first clause should explicitly restrict to separable maximal subfields, since Galois closure is only relevant in that setting and the paper immediately discusses maximal separable subfields in this context.
The base field should be stated explicitly: A is a central F-division algebra of degree n (equivalently, dim_F A = n^2 in the paper’s setup).
The Galois closure should be specified as the Galois closure of K/F inside a separable closure F_sep of F.
"Smallest" should be made precise as minimal order among finite groups occurring in this way; the paper uses the plural "group(s)" because there may be several minimal groups of the same order.

The question should make clear that one is determining the minimal groups realizable by Galois closures of maximal subfields of the given algebra A, not arbitrary minimal Galois splitting groups unrelated to maximal subfields.
refined_question: Let A be a central F-division algebra of degree n (so dim_F A = n^2). Among all finite groups G for which there exists a separable maximal subfield K \subset A with [K:F] = n such that the Galois closure L of K/F inside a separable closure F_sep of F satisfies Gal(L/F) \cong G, determine the group(s) of minimal order. In particular, must every central F-division algebra A of degree n contain a separable maximal subfield K whose Galois closure over F has Galois group A_n?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 2.4. The subsection "Smallest Galois splitting fields" first explains that the issue is to minimize the degree/order of finite Galois splitting groups, defines what it means for a finite group to split a central simple algebra, and then states exactly the problem about groups arising from the Galois closure of a maximal subfield, with the highlighted special question about the alternating group A_n. Section 0 supplies the background that makes this formulation natural by linking crossed products, maximal tori/maximal subfields, and finite Galois splitting fields. So the sharp paper-faithful target is Problem 2.4, not the adjacent Problem 2.5 on abelian splitting groups and not the later admissibility reformulation.
